articles.title: The Best New Products of August 2026: Stanley, Ninja, Cécred and More
articles.summary: Some of the top new products in August 2026 are the Stanley Vitalize Tote, Cécred’s first face product and the 2nd edition of Bose’s QuietComfort headphones.
articles.body: This story is part of NBC Selected’s New & Notable column, where we highlight our favorite product launches. We will continuously update this article throughout the month with new releases we think you should know about. Apparel and footwear launches Hoka designed a unisex lifestyle version of its popular Clifton running and walking sneaker, giving you the same level of comfort and support in a stylish, street-ready shoe. It has lots of soft cushioning, grippy rubber outsoles and reflective laces, plus raised textured and mesh details on the upper (the fabric part that covers the top of your foot) to give it some flair. The Clifton UTL is currently only available in one color with additional seasonal shades dropping throughout September. Mary Janes are having a moment lately, especially those from brands that traditionally make sports shoes. Teva is the latest company to get in on the trend with its Ampsole Gaila Mary Jane, which is a closed-toe version of its bestselling Hurricane Ampsole Gaila sandal. The shoe has an elevated platform, a grippy outsole and a cushy footbed. There’s also a buckle closure that makes the shoes easy to put on and take off. The Ghost Amp is Brooks’ latest lightweight running shoe made for daily jogs and fast tempo workouts. They have a springy, propulsive feel, especially in the forefoot, helping you pop off your toes and roll into your next stride. The shoes are also made with soft cushioning and a balanced amount of support from heel to toe to keep your feet stable. You can buy the shoes in men’s and women’s standard and wide sizes. Low-profile sneakers have been popular all year, and the Ivy Sneaker is Rothy’s take on the footwear trend. The shoes have a collegiate style, with their cleat-like rubber outsoles and vegan leather details, but they also have all the elements you know and love about Rothy’s: the cushioned footbed is comfortable, and you can throw them in the washing machine. The Ivy Sneaker, which is only available in women’s sizes, is made from Rothy’s ReVelvet fabric, a soft material that looks similar to suede. Nobull’s Recharge Slides are great to wear after a workout, standing for hours or doing lots of walking. The shoes are specifically designed for recovery with soft cushioning and contours in the footbed that support your arches — Nobull says it decided exactly where to put the contours by evaluating 3D foot scans to ensure they were anatomically correct. The shoe’s footbed is also textured to add stability along with the strap. The Recharge Slide comes in men’s and women’s sizes. “My feet breathe a sigh of relief when I put these slides on after running or wearing restrictive shoes all day at work,” says NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin (the brand sent her a pair to test). “They don’t slip off when I’m moving around at home or walking my dog down the block, and I appreciate that the cushioning is soft enough to encourage my feet to release tension, but not so soft that I sink into it. I love the textured footbed, too — it definitely prevents my feet from sliding around, and it feels like a little massage.” Lake’s BalanceKnit fabric is made from a material that has naturally derived minerals built-in — they respond to changes in body temperature so heat escapes when you’re warm and stays in when you’re cold, according to the brand. Lake used the fabric to create its first line of women’s thermoregulating pajamas, which are available in six initial styles. You can get a nightgown, shorts and short-sleeve shirt set, tank top and pants set, shorts and tank top set, long sleeve shirt and pants set, and short-sleeve shirt and pants set. Malin wore Lake’s BalanceKnit pajamas for a few nights over the past two weeks after the brand sent her the tank top and shorts set. “As a hot sleeper, I’m always looking for pajamas that keep me cool overnight, and these delivered in the middle of a New York City heatwave,” she says. “The fabric is so soft and cozy, and it successfully kept me from overheating for hours, so I was happy to lounge around and get under the covers (with the AC on of course) in the set.” Other notable apparel and footwear launches: Hill House Home Eden Row Capsule Collection Kizik Sierra Chelsea New Balance SuperComp Rebel and SuperComp Elite v6 Saucony ProGrid V2 Mule Tommy John Second Skin Bra Collection: Wireless T-Shirt, Light Support and Pullover V-Neck Vera Bradley Mini Bags: The Mini Clara and The Maisie Z Supply Five-Pocket Premium Denim Collection Tech launches Bose’s QuietComfort Headphones are one of the best over-ear options you can buy, and with the second edition, the brand added new features to make them even better. They now have improved noise cancellation, which you can opt to completely turn off in the app, and come with Bose Immersive Audio, a feature that gives you access to Cinema Mode to make dialogue clearer while watching videos. There’s also two-way USB-C audio to enhance your video call experience and let you use the headphones while they’re plugged in to charge. Plus, the overall design of the headphones makes them feel more comfortable and look more modern: Their headband has smooth adjustable sliders, there’s extra plush cushioning throughout and the earcups are oval-shaped. Many NBC Selected team members are fans of Shokz’s open earbuds, and the brand just added two new models to its lineup. First, OpenRun Air 2 is meant for you to wear while running, cycling, hiking and doing outdoor training. It’s the newest version of Shokz’s signature headphones, and it’s smaller in size and lighter in weight than the previous iteration, plus it has updated hooks that better fit the ears’ curves, which help them stay in place. The Open Run Air 2, which is water-resistant, also got performance upgrades to improve the listening experience, and its battery now lasts longer. You can control the headphones using the buttons on the sides while relying on the AI-powered microphone to reduce noise while you’re talking. The OpenFit Air 2 is mainly a lifestyle open earbud, but you can wear it for light to medium-intensity workouts, too. It’s officially the lightest model in Shokz’s OpenFit collection, according to the brand, and more comfortable, stable and portable than the first version. Its sound has improved so everything you hear is fuller and more dynamic, and there’s less sound leakage when you’re in public spaces. Shokz also upgraded these headphones’ pressure-sensitive controls so they’re not triggered by stray hair or sweat droplets, according to the brand. The Hatch Sleep Clock isn’t just a customizable sunrise alarm clock and sound machine, it’s also a sleep tracker that uses motion sensors to track your movements and breathing patterns throughout the night with 97 percent accuracy, according to the brand. You put it on your nightstand so it’s facing your body, and in the morning, the brand’s app gives you an overview of how you slept. As the app learns your sleep patterns, it recommends ways you can improve your slumber, too. New features of the latest Hatch clock also include a built-in bedside light, and, like other versions, it has a phone-free design — once you set up your wake and sleep routines in the app, you can exclusively control the device with its buttons. Other notable tech launches: Belkin SoundForm Play Active Noise Cancelling Headphones for KidsSegway S2 Kids Self-Balancing Scooter and Sam’s Club-exclusive C2 SE E-Scooter Skullcandy Crusher 1080 ANC Headphones Beauty launches Tower 28’s foundation is a companion to its Swipe Serum concealer, and it’s suitable for sensitive and acne-prone skin. It has a non-comedogenic, non-acnegenic formula that includes hydrating ingredients like fermented oat, squalane and glycerin to keep skin from drying out throughout the day, according to the brand. The foundation’s key ingredient, however, is portulaca extract, which is anti-inflammatory and anti-microbial that helps to soothe breakouts and irritation. It has a medium-buildable coverage and can be worn for up to 16 hours. It launched alongside the brand’s first-ever makeup tools, two complexion brushes: the Big Blender Brush for larger areas and the Baby Blender Brush for precision blending. NBC Selected updates editor Mili Godio, who has very sensitive, acne-prone skin, says this foundation is her latest obsession. “I can wear it all day without having to worry about irritation or random breakouts. It has a dewy finish, which is great for my dry skin, and it makes my makeup look smooth and even,” she says. “I love applying it with the brand’s Big Blender Brush since it blends the foundation quickly and evenly. However, the texture is a little on the oilier side, so if you have oily skin, you might want to reconsider.” Medicube is one of our favorite Korean skin care brands, and its new sheet mask is formulated to treat fine lines and boost your skin’s overall radiation. NAD+ helps improve elasticity, resulting in firmer, smoother skin, while collagen keeps skin hydrated, which helps produce the infamous “glass skin” look that K-beauty is known for. The gel mask hugs the skin and has a cooling feel that soothes any potential irritation, and can be used for three to four hours at a time or overnight for best results, according to the brand. Summer Fridays launched its first body care line this month. The line includes butter balms, belly balms and body mists in delicious scents like pink guava, vanilla and pistachio milk. If you can’t decide what product (or scent) to try out first, you can purchase mini bundles like a body mist trio, body butter trio and this body essentials set that comes with the brand’s viral lip butter balm, too. Cécred has finally launched a face product, but it’s not what you may think. The latest drop, a Restoring Lash & Brow Builder, expands on the brand’s Restoring Edge Drops to visibly improve the density of your eyelashes and eyebrows in only 30 days, according to the brand. The serum includes the brand’s biopeptide blend, which increases protein production and results in longer, thicker lashes and brows. It’s great for thinning caused by hormonal changes, over-plucking and more, and has a gentle formula that can be used daily, even by those with sensitive skin. This new styling tool from Pattern Beauty has ceramic-coated plates that vibrate at up to 12,000 vibrations per minute for smooth, straight styling in less passes (meaning less heat damage), according to the brand. It includes an LCD display that shows real-time temperature, along with 14 customizable heat settings and a 60-minute auto-shutoff timer. The flat iron also has cool tip guards for added control and precision while styling. It launched alongside two new hair care products from the brand: Blow Out Primer and Detox Shampoo. Tangle Teezer spent more than five years overhauling its classic hairbrush to create the Complete Carebrush, which comes in three versions to suit different hair types: fine hair (softest bristles), straight to wavy hair (medium bristles) and curly to coily hair (firmest bristles). Each brush has two tiers of teeth that are arranged diagonally, letting hair flow through at any angle to prevent breakage: one tier has longer, oval-shaped teeth to massage your scalp and smooth your hair, while the other has shorter, triangular teeth to detangle without damaging hair. Malin has been a Tangle Teezer fan for years and says she immediately noticed the difference between the old and new brush the first time she used it (the brand sent her the one for curly to coily hair). “Beyond its paddle being bigger to cover more hair at once, it’s noticeably firmer as the brand describes — the bristles don’t bend or splay as they work their way through my thick hair, and the brush’s body is sturdier overall,” she says. “I use it for detangling knots in the shower after conditioning, which it successfully does without pulling at my hair or irritating my scalp.” Olaplex’s first-ever hairspray has a 96-hour hold, according to the brand, leaving your style fully set and fizz-free. The formula includes encapsulated peptides to help repair broken bonds in your hair strands while strengthening your hair overall, along with polymers that control and keep frizz away. Malin has been testing Olaplex’s latest styling product for about two weeks since the brand sent it to her. “I use hairspray to tame frizz after touching up a blowout or refreshing day-two curls, but I hate when it makes my hair crunchy,” she says. “Olaplex’s doesn’t do that at all. It smooths out my hair and keeps styles in place without making my hair look or feel stiff, and it smells incredible, which is an added bonus.” Other notable beauty launches: Aestura Atobarrier365 Capsule TonerBanu Deep Drench Moisturizer for Acne-Prone SkinBubble Clean Landing Daily Purifying SprayCeraVe Invisible Mineral Sunscreen SPF 50Cetaphil Nourishing & Hydrating Lotion and Nourishing & Hydrating Cream Charlotte Tilbury Airbrush Flawless Blur Loose Setting Powder and Airbrush Flawless Blush Blur Ciele Lip & Protect SPF 60+ Lipstick Dezi Skin Pore Choices Plant-based Mucin Repair Mist Dieux Firm Revival HydroRetinal Firming Serum Dieux Firm Revival HydroRetinal Firming SerumDND Gel I’m the Captain Now! It sucks up both solid and liquid spills and messes, so it’s suitable for cleaning food, dirt, mud and pet hair, according to the brand. Safe on hardwood, tile, laminate, vinyl, stainless steel and more, the appliance comes with an extendable cleaning wand, which you can use on hard-to-reach and elevated areas, including baseboards, walls and backsplashes. The wand sprays the cleaning solution on the surface and then sucks it up, just like with a regular vacuum. The appliance also has a self-cleaning feature that you can use by putting it back on the dock and allowing it to do a rinse wash. In fact, shoppers say the self-cleaning feature is one of the best facets of the appliance, in addition to how well it cleans hard surfaces. It provides up to more than 100 square feet of circulation and the air moves up to nearly 20 miles per hour, according to the brand. Shoppers who reviewed the fan also say that it’s very quiet and almost inaudible on the first few low speeds, and that even when it makes some sound, it provides relaxing background noise. The Ninja HydraSense is a water filtration system that fits on a table, countertop or other household flat surface — no need for fiddling with plumbing. The filter removes up to 99 percent of contaminants in water like PFAS (also known as “forever chemicals”), other types of microplastics and carcinogens, but without removing minerals that impact the flavor, according to Ninja. It also has a 120-gallon filter, so you can clean about six months of water before it needs replacing, and it comes with a stainless steel Ninja Thirsti water bottle that lets you take your water on the go. This automatic Cricut heat press has an extra-large 15-by-15-inch heat plate, so you can use it for bigger projects, like customizing large items of clothing and blankets with iron-on designs. It’s also more powerful than the previous iteration: It provides up to 220 pounds of pressure and gets as hot as 410 degrees Fahrenheit. The tote has a combination of features you’d find on both a work tote and a cooler: It has a laptop sleeve on the inside with a velcro strap, multiple pockets and pouches inside, and an insulated cooler compartment on the bottom (perfect for canned drinks, snacks and sandwiches). Arguably its best feature is the pair of pockets — one on each side — that tightly hold multiple sizes of Stanley water bottles and tumblers, including 30- and 40-ounce ones with handles. Dagne Dover’s Andre Backpack is a cross between a traditional backpack and a work tote, making it ideal for the office, classes, the gym and traveling. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans considers herself a bonafide backpack hater (when it comes to pairing with work clothes) and she said she would actually wear this to the office. Calpak’s Vault Collection is a lineup of suitcases made from ultra-durable aluminum material. The suitcases, which come in carry-on, medium and large checked-luggage sizes, have wheels that spin 360 degrees, an adjustable handle, a removable divider panel on the inside, a built-in TSA-approved lock and additional handles on the side for easy handling in overhead bins and luggage racks. Doona also added a larger UPF 50+ canopy, a step-on/step-off brake system and an improved shock absorption system for a smoother ride. Plus, there’s a soft opening mechanism when you’re transitioning from car seat to stroller mode. This bottle warmer has two separate modes that makes it great for combo feeding: one setting is specifically designed for breastmilk and uses a gentle water bath to warm or defrost it, and the other uses steam to warm up formula and baby food in about two minutes, according to the brand. The warmer accommodates nearly all bottles, milk storage bags and baby food jars, and it automatically shuts off when it’s done. The new version of Lalo’s high chair stems from real parent feedback. The legs tuck in tighter, which helps those with little kitchen space, and it has both an adjustable back and footrest, making starting solids easier and safer, according to the brand. The chair also has silicone straps with a magnetic buckle and a tray that you can easily remove using one hand. It adjusts five different ways to make it functional as your child grows; it converts into a booster seat, child chair, play chair and play stool. Earlier this month, model and influencer Olivia Culpo launched her Target-exclusive brand, Picolette by Olivia Culpo, a 60-piece collection filled with adorably timeless baby clothing and accessories. Some of the collection’s bestsellers so far include a floral long-sleeve romper, plush stuffed animal, silicone sippy and snack cups, and this gingham-patterned case for baby wipes. Take more control over pumping with this portable breast pump, which is an upgraded version of the BabyBuddha 2.0 that has an additional pumping mode and more comfort settings to choose from. It also comes with a complete sizing kit, so you won’t need to purchase an additional tool to make sure the pump is comfortable. articles.title: A Russian missile and drone barrage kills at least 14 in Ukraine’s Kyiv region
articles.summary: Moscow’s forces have intensified their ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv in recent months, exploiting Ukraine’s chronic shortage of U.S.-made Patriot air defense interceptors.
articles.body: Russia pounded the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, and the surrounding region with scores of missiles and drones in a nighttime aerial attack that lasted for hours and killed at least 14 people, officials said Thursday. Moscow’s forces have in recent months intensified their ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv, exploiting Ukraine’s chronic shortage of U.S.-made Patriot air defense interceptors, the sole weapon in its arsenal able to shoot down ballistic missiles. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has pleaded for countries to send more Patriot interceptors, but international stockpiles are low amid the Iran war and Ukraine’s more than four-year fight against Russia’s all-out invasion. Russia’s overnight barrage also included cruise missiles and fast-flying, jet-powered drones that put further strain on air defenses, the Ukrainian air force said. Explosions boomed across the city in the dark. Kyiv was the primary target, but hits were recorded at 28 locations across the country, according to the air force. About 40 people were wounded, Zelenskyy said, as air raid warnings remained in place until after dawn. Russia and Ukraine have battered each other with drones and missiles as their armies struggle to gain the upper hand on the 780-mile front line, where huge numbers of drones are pinning down troops. Ukraine has attempted to shift the war onto Russian soil through long-range drone strikes on oil facilities and other infrastructure. The Russian Defense Ministry said Thursday morning that air defenses shot down 726 Ukrainian drones overnight over a number of Russian regions, annexed Crimea and the Black and Azov seas, in one of Ukraine’s biggest aerial attacks of the war. There were no immediate reports of damage or casualties. Russia’s relentless onslaught on Kyiv has spooked other European countries, especially those bordering Ukraine, which fear what Russian President Vladimir Putin might have in store for the continent. As the Russian attack on Kyiv unfolded, the Polish Armed Forces Operational Command activated its military aviation operations, ground-based air defense systems and its radar reconnaissance. Polish and other NATO military aircraft were deployed to monitor the country’s airspace, Polish news agency PAP reported. Romania’s Defense Ministry said that an unidentified drone crashed and caught fire in an uninhabited area near the border with Ukraine. Two Spanish F-18 jets, deployed on an air policing mission in Romania, were scrambled after 2 a.m. local time to monitor a group of “air targets” near the border, the ministry said. Also, Moldova’s Defense Ministry said that its airspace was breached by an unauthorized drone. Russia’s overnight strikes hit 12 locations across Kyiv’s Darnytskyi, Sviatoshynskyi and Solomianskyi districts, damaging residential buildings, a medical facility and an educational institution. Emergency crews were at the scene and pulled people out from under the rubble. Larysa Bondaruk, 60, sat on the ground, holding her cat, Chanel, which had been rescued by firefighters. With tears in her eyes, she said that her neighbor’s grandson had been trapped under the rubble and died. Her apartment was badly damaged. “A rocket hit the roof. It was incredibly loud. Immediately, debris and doors were blown out. There were columns of smoke, columns of fire, screams, crying and despair,” she said. “Two people were killed in our building, but the rescuers responded quickly and professionally. I am grateful to them for that.” In Solomianskyi district, the top two floors of a nine-story residential building were destroyed, and fires broke out on other floors. People were also trapped in two residential buildings and a school shelter.

articles.title: Dr. Furlan (PSD) participa de caminhadas em Macapá e Santana | G1
articles.standfirst: O candidato do PSD cumpriu três agendas nesta segunda-feira (31). O político participou de reuniões com candidatos e militância na capital.
articles.summary: Dr. Furlan, candidato ao governo do Amapá, realizou caminhadas no bairro Infraero II, em Macapá, e em Santana, além de se reunir com a militância nesta segunda-feira (31).
articles.body:
Candidato ao governo do Amapá, Dr. Furlan (PSD) — Foto: Maria Clara Prudêncio/g1

O candidato ao governo do Amapá, Dr. Furlan ( PSD ), cumpriu três agendas de campanha nesta segunda-feira (31), em Macapá e Santana .

Pela manhã, o político participou de uma caminhada no bairro do Infraero II, em Macapá . À tarde, o candidato esteve em uma caminhada no bairro Comercial, em Santana . À noite, Dr. Furlan se reuniu com candidatos e militância em Macapá .

A campanha eleitoral começou no dia 16 de agosto em todo o país. Desde então, os candidatos podem realizar propaganda nas ruas e na internet.

A propaganda eleitoral começou na sexta-feira (28) na televisão e no rádio e segue até 1º de outubro. O primeiro turno das eleições acontece em 4 de outubro.

Às segundas, quartas e sextas-feiras, são exibidas as campanhas dos candidatos a senador, deputado estadual e governador. A propaganda eleitoral gratuita é considerada fundamental para atrair eleitores e ampliar a projeção dos candidatos.

articles.title: Secretário do Exército dos EUA pede demissão, diz jornal | G1
articles.standfirst: Reportagem do Wall Street Journal cita tensões entre Dan Driscoll e o secretário da Guerra de Donald Trump, Pete Hegseth.
articles.summary: Reportagem do Wall Street Journal cita tensões entre Dan Driscoll e o secretário da Guerra de Donald Trump, Pete Hegseth.
articles.body:
O Secretário do Exército, Dan Driscoll, presta depoimento durante uma audiência no Senado americano em maio de 2026. — Foto: Nathan Posner/Reuters

O secretário do Exército dos Estados Unidos , Dan Driscoll, pediu demissão do cargo, informou o jornal The Wall Street Journal nesta segunda-feira (31). Tensões com o secretário de Guerra, Pete Hegseth, motivaram a saída.

Segundo a imprensa americana, Driscoll e Hegseth têm entrado em atritos frequentes desde que o segundo assumiu o cargo, em janeiro de 2025. O secretário de Guerra é aliado do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump.

A tensão entre Driscoll e Hegseth teria resultado na demissão do chefe do Estado-Maior do Exército, general Randy George , em abril.

Driscoll e George eram parceiros próximos, segundo o WSJ, e desenvolviam juntos projetos de renovação tecnológica no Exército. Os dois também viajaram juntos para a Ucrânia antes da demissão do general.

A remoção de George provocou críticas a Hegseth entre deputados e senadores do próprio partido, os republicanos.

Em comunicado enviado ao WSJ, a Casa Branca elogiou o trabalho de Driscoll. A porta-voz Anna Kelly afirmou que o secretário foi eficaz na implementação da agenda de Trump, na preparação das Forças Armadas para operações militares e nas negociações entre Rússia e Ucrânia.

O secretário de Defesa dos Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth, fala durante uma declaração à imprensa ao chegar para uma reunião de ministros da defesa da OTAN na sede da organização em Bruxelas, quinta-feira, 18 de junho de 2026. — Foto: AP Photo/Virginia Mayo

Hegseth chegou a servir no Exército dos EUA e atuou no Iraque e no Afeganistão, mas fez carreira como âncora do canal de TV conservador Fox News antes de ser indicado por Trump para comandar o Pentágono.

A chegada de Hegseth à chefia do Departamento de Guerra foi vista com desconfiança pela liderança militar dos EUA, composta em grande parte por funcionários de carreira.

No primeiro semestre de 2026, o secretário passou a promover uma "limpa" na alta cúpula das Forças Armadas . Uma reformulação militar ampla é incomum na história do país, ainda mais em momentos de conflito aberto, como a guerra contra o Irã.

articles.body:
Eleições 2026: Candidatos ao governo do Piauí — Foto: Montagem/g1

Os candidatos ao Governo do Piauí cumpriram agenda de campanha em Teresina e em municípios do interior do estado.

Entre os compromissos, estiveram caminhadas, panfletagens, reuniões políticas, encontros com lideranças e apoiadores, além de visitas, gravação de podcast e conteúdos para as redes sociais.

O primeiro turno das eleições será realizado no dia 4 de outubro. Já o segundo turno, caso necessário, está marcado para 25 de outubro.

Veja, abaixo, como foi o dia de campanha de cada candidato, em ordem alfabética:

Durante a manhã, a candidata gravou um podcast e teve uma reunião política. No período da tarde, se reuniu com a equipe de comunicação, participou da gravação de conteúdos da campanha e, posteriormente, teve um novo encontro político.

À noite, ela participou de reuniões com simpatizantes e apoiadores.

Durante a manhã, o candidato participou de uma reunião de alinhamento da campanha.

À tarde, ele realizou uma caminhada no bairro Alto da Ressurreição, na Zona Sudeste de Teresina.

Durante a manhã, o candidato realizou panfletagem de material de campanha no bairro Ininga, além de uma visita à Universidade Federal do Piauí (UFPI) e ao Restaurante Universitário da instituição.

À tarde, ele participou de uma caminhada e panfletagem de material de campanha no bairro Ininga, na Zona Leste de Teresina.

Na manhã, o candidato passou pelo Centro de Teresina em caminhada, com percurso pela Rua Paissandu e pela região comercial. Depois, teve uma reunião com a coordenação política da campanha, conversou com comerciantes do bairro Vermelha e das áreas próximas à Avenida Miguel Rosa e almoçou com apoiadores.

Já no período da tarde, se reuniu novamente com a coordenação da campanha, produziu conteúdos para as redes sociais e participou de um adesivaço na sede do partido. À noite, o candidato participou de reuniões com simpatizantes e apoiadores.

Pela manhã, o candidato participou dos festejos de São Raimundo Nonato, na Igreja Matriz de Miguel Leão, e, em seguida, se reuniu com lideranças políticas no município. À tarde, teve um encontro com lideranças políticas em Teresina.

À noite, participou da procissão de São Raimundo Nonato, em União , e, depois, se reuniu com uma liderança política e apoiadores em Teresina em dois compromissos distintos.

A candidata não teve agenda de campanha nesta segunda. Ela sofreu um AVC hemorrágico e está internada em Teresina.

Na parte da manhã, o candidato esteve na Praça Rio Branco, no Centro de Teresina, onde realizou panfletagem de material de campanha. Depois, passou pelos Restaurantes Universitários da UFPI para distribuir material aos estudantes.

No período da tarde, participou de uma caminhada na Praça do Liceu Piauiense, no Centro da capital.

Durante a manhã, o candidato percorreu a avenida principal do bairro Promorar em caminhada e, posteriormente, visitou o polo de peças e serviços do bairro Tabuleta.

À tarde, o candidato participou de uma sabatina em um veículo de comunicação.

A candidata não informou a agenda de campanha para esta segunda-feira (31).

Na manhã, o candidato esteve na Praça do Fripisa, no Centro de Teresina, onde distribuiu material de campanha.

No período da tarde, voltou ao local para continuar a panfletagem e conversar com eleitores.

articles.title: Menores morrem em bombardeio de governo a guerrilheiros na Colômbia | G1
articles.standfirst: Dois adolescentes de 15 anos e outros dois de 16 teriam morrido em ataques aéreos na Amazônia e na fronteira com a Venezuela, onde grupos armados disputam as receitas do narcotráfico, da mineração ilegal e da extorsão.
articles.summary: Dois adolescentes de 15 anos e outros dois de 16 teriam morrido em ataques aéreos na Amazônia e na fronteira com a Venezuela, onde grupos armados atuam.
articles.body:
Abelardo De La Espriella participa de vigília em homenagem às vítimas de terremoto na Colâmbia, em 28 de agosto de 2026 — Foto: Raul Arboleda/AFP

Quatro menores de idade morreram nos primeiros bombardeios ordenados pelo recém-empossado governo do direitista Abelardo de la Espriella em áreas controladas por guerrilheiros, informou à agência France Presse (AFP) uma fonte da autoridade forense nesta segunda-feira (31).

Dois adolescentes de 15 anos e outros dois de 16 teriam morrido em ataques aéreos na Amazônia e na fronteira com a Venezuela, onde grupos armados disputam as receitas do narcotráfico, da mineração ilegal e da extorsão.

"Os bandidos que durante décadas recrutaram menores para transformá-los em combatentes ou em escudos humanos devem pagar por esses crimes que violam o Direito Humanitário", disse o presidente no X.

Desde que tomou posse, em 7 de agosto, os bombardeios ordenados por De la Espriella deixaram pelo menos 26 mortos, em meio à pior onda de violência da última década.

O presidente chegou ao poder com a promessa de enfrentar sem trégua guerrilheiros e narcotraficantes com o apoio de seus aliados Estados Unidos e Israel.

"Todo o meu apoio às operações militares que combatem (...) os grupos narcoterroristas", acrescentou.

As operações foram realizadas contra a guerrilha Exército de Libertação Nacional (ELN) na região do Catatumbo, na fronteira com a Venezuela, e contra uma dissidência das extintas Farc em Guaviare, no sul do país.

Nos últimos anos, as organizações ampliaram seu contingente e controle territorial, segundo analistas e fontes militares.

No ano passado, foram registrados 428 casos de recrutamento de menores por grupos armados, segundo a Defensoria do Povo.

Neste ano, até 31 de julho, já foram registrados 97 casos.

De la Espriella informou nesta segunda-feira sobre um terceiro bombardeio em Guaviare contra outra dissidência das Farc comandada por Iván Mordisco, o guerrilheiro mais procurado da Colômbia .

Oito integrantes de suas fileiras foram mortos, segundo o presidente, e ainda não se sabe se havia menores de idade.

Organizações de defesa dos direitos humanos alertam para o impacto dos bombardeios sobre as crianças vítimas de recrutamento em áreas pobres e com presença mínima do Estado.

articles.title: Candidatos ao governo do DF propõem viadutos e melhorias no transporte | G1
articles.standfirst: Agenda foi marcada por entrevistas e reuniões com lojistas. Rodoviária do Plano Piloto esteve no centro das ações de campanha.
articles.summary: Candidatos ao governo do DF focam em mobilidade urbana e reuniões com lojistas na Rodoviária do Plano Piloto para apresentar propostas de infraestrutura e economia.
articles.body:
A agenda dos candidatos ao governos do DF foi marcada por entrevistas e reuniões com o setor produtivo.

Durante esta segunda-feira (31), representantes estiveram na Rodoviária do Plano Piloto e outras regiões centrais do DF.

A mobilidade urbana e apoio ao comércio foram alguns dos destaques da campanha.

O candidato José Roberto Arruda, do PSD, esteve em sabatina com representantes do setor produtivo. O evento ocorreu no auditório da Câmara dos Dirigentes Lojistas, no SIA.

Durante discurso, o ex-governador prometeu parceria com o setor privado para qualificação da mão de obra. Segundo ele, a falta de segurança é um dos principais problemas enfrentados pelos comerciantes.

Arruda prometeu ainda que, caso eleito, vai incentivar pequenos negócios por meio do BRB.

“Eles não têm as garantias que os grandes bancos exigem. Mas, na nossa experiência, pobre paga a conta, quem deixa de pagar às vezes é o rico. É preciso que o banco tenha facilidade de fazer fomento às startups, às micro e pequenas empresas, para que eles comecem os seus negócios e possam evoluir”, afirmou.

A deputada distrital e candidata Paula Belmonte (PSDB) cumpriu agenda na rodoviária do Plano Piloto. Ela também esteve na sabatina com lojistas, onde falou sobre capacitação profissional e educação financeira nas escolas.

“A nossa proposta, como governo do Distrito Federal, é dar empregabilidade para as pessoas, capacitação para pessoas, as pessoas precisam ser empregadas, e para que elas possam estar empregadas, a gente tem que fomentar o setor produtivo”, declarou.

Belmonte também prometeu trabalhar junto à Companhia Imobiliária de Brasília (Terracap) na regulação de terras para os produtores rurais. A deputada afirmou que, caso eleita, vai expandir vias e criar um anel rodoviário.

Representante do PSB na disputa ao governo, Ricardo Cappelli iniciou a segunda com entrevista no Setor de Rádio e TV Sul.

Na saída, o candidato falou que, se for eleito governador, pretende fazer mais investimentos na Companhia de Saneamento Ambiental do Distrito Federal (Caesb). Cappelli citou problemas com buracos e vazamentos, e destacou impactos para o meio ambiente.

Cappelli voltou a criticar o déficit de profissionais na saúde. “Qual o problema que os médicos não estão vindo? É o salário? Vamos rediscutir o salário, porque o que não pode é deixar as pessoas sofrendo na fila da saúde como estão hoje. Tem mais de um milhão de consultas e exames na fila”, declarou.

O candidato também esteve na Rodoviária, onde falou sobre investimentos para o BRT e ônibus expressos para Sobradinho, Planaltina, Arapoanga e Fercal.

O candidato do PT, Leandro Grass, começou o dia com caminhada pelo comércio do Núcleo Bandeirante. Ele destacou a importância da tradição da região administrativa que, segundo ele, tem sofrido com a falta de investimentos.

Grass prometeu que, se eleito, vai implementar espaços de convivência para a população 60%. Ele defendeu ainda o fortalecimento das práticas de saúde para a população e o combate à violência contra idosos.

Em agenda na Rodoviária, o candidato prometeu ainda a implementação da tarifa zero no transporte público.

“A gente precisa fazer primeiro uma mudança da relação do governo com as empresas que hoje recebem muito dinheiro e prestam um serviço ruim. Aí a gente faz o que tem que ser feito: ampliar as linhas de ônibus, ampliar os horários das linhas para a gente poder também ter a tarifa zero, que a gente quer implementar gradualmente aqui no DF até o final do nosso governo. Ônibus de graça em todas as linhas”, declarou.

A governadora Celina Leão participou de entrevista em emissora de rádio. Na saída, a candidata à reeleição falou sobre levar moradias ao Setor Comercial Sul.

A proposta é que o setor vire uma área de produção cultural, atraindo o público mais jovem. Segundo a candidata, a medida deve movimentar a região e afastar problemas relacionados ao esvaziamento.

Celina também esteve no Guará, onde prometeu a implementação de quadras e parques. Em visita ao Park Sul, região vizinha, ela falou sobre a construção de um viaduto para reduzir os engarrafamentos na região.

“Não adianta também a gente só investir [na região] e não ter um novo viaduto para escoamento, porque você está tendo um adensamento muito grande aqui. O problema do trânsito você tem que trabalhar com perspectiva de futuro, porque tem novos empreendimentos chegando aqui”, afirmou.

articles.body:
Os candidatos ao governo do Acre cumpriram compromissos de campanha nesta segunda-feira (31). Entre as atividades do dia estiveram caminhadas e encontros com apoiadores.

Alan Rick (Republicanos) participou de uma caminhada na regional Vila Acre pela manhã , conversou com moradores e comerciantes e participou de gravações. Durante o encontro com a população, ele disse que pretende investir em mobilidade urbana, infraestrutura e apoio aos pequenos produtores rurais do região.

"Temos um projeto no nosso plano de governo de viabilidade, uma mobilidade urbana. E aqui é uma área que realmente nós precisamos pensar no modelo de viaduto, um modelo de mobilidade que melhore o fluxo do trânsito", afirmou.

Mailza Assis (PP) gravou programa eleitoral, em agenda fechada. Ela terá ainda um encontro com mulheres às 18h30.

A Rede Amazônica iniciou nesta segunda a cobertura das agendas dos candidatos ao governo estadual, conforme os critérios definidos com representantes dos partidos e coligações.

A frequência da cobertura segue o desempenho de cada candidato na pesquisa Quaest mais recente, conforme acordo firmado com representantes dos partidos e coligações.

Candidatos que registraram 5% ou mais das intenções de voto terão a agenda exibida de segunda a sexta-feira. Para aqueles que aparecem com 3% ou 4%, a cobertura será feita duas vezes por semana.

Candidatos com 1% ou 2% terão a agenda exibida uma vez por semana, exclusivamente aos sábados. Já os que não pontuaram na pesquisa terão a agenda exibida a cada duas semanas, também aos sábados.

O candidato ao governo de Alagoas JHC ( PSDB ) participou, na manhã desta segunda-feira (31), de uma sabatina promovida pela Federação das Indústrias do Estado de Alagoas (Fiea). Durante a tarde, ele fez gravações para o guia eleitoral e não teve outras atividades de campanha previstas para o restante do dia.

JHC chegou à sede da federação acompanhado de assessores e da equipe de comunicação. A sabatina foi realizada em um auditório no sexto andar do prédio, mas a imprensa não foi autorizada a acompanhar o encontro.

Entre as propostas apresentadas pelo candidato para o setor industrial estão a ampliação da atividade industrial em Alagoas e a capacitação de trabalhadores por meio de cursos técnicos e profissionalizantes.

JHC também defendeu investimentos em infraestrutura para atrair empresas ligadas à tecnologia e destacou o potencial de Alagoas na produção de gás e de energias renováveis.

“Todo o potencial que a gente tem de gás, energia eólica e solar, que são consumidos pelos data centers, e todas essas estratégias de ecossistemas de tecnologia dependem muito dessa infraestrutura necessária para vir para o estado. Então, vamos pensar a Alagoas do futuro, o Nordeste do futuro e o Brasil do futuro que nós queremos”, afirmou.

Após a agenda na Fiea, o candidato dedicou a tarde às gravações para o programa eleitoral. Não foram divulgados outros compromissos públicos de campanha para esta segunda-feira.

articles.title: Leonardo DiCaprio e amigos ficam em fazenda de luxo no Pantanal de MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Ator está em Miranda com namorada e amigos para conhecer iniciativas de conservação da fauna e da flora do Pantanal.
articles.summary: Ator está em Miranda com amigos para conhecer iniciativas de conservação da fauna e da flora do Pantanal
articles.body:
Leonardo Dicaprio visita Pantanal de MS — Foto: Reprodução

O ator Leonardo DiCaprio e um grupo de amigos estão no Pantanal de Mato Grosso do Sul para conhecer iniciativas voltadas à conservação da fauna e da flora do bioma. A visita ocorre na Fazenda Caiman, em Miranda , município localizado na região do Pantanal sul-mato-grossense.

De acordo com apuração do g1 , além de DiCaprio, fazem parte do grupo a namorada do ator, Vittoria Ceretti, Laura Ruth Harrier, Weston Sechrest, Hillel Nahmad, Todd Graves, Rodrigo Medeiros, Raul Guterres e Camila Klabin.

Até o momento, não foram feitos registros públicos no local, por questões de privacidade e segurança do grupo.

A presença de DiCaprio no Pantanal ocorre devido ao interesse do ator por pautas ambientais. O grupo está conhecendo iniciativas que desenvolvem pesquisas e ações de conservação na região.

A Fazenda Caiman serve de base para pesquisas e atividades de instituições que estudam espécies do Pantanal. Pesquisadores, biólogos e equipes de projetos ambientais atuam no monitoramento de espécies e em estudos relacionados ao ecossistema pantaneiro.

Além das atividades de pesquisa, algumas iniciativas permitem que visitantes acompanhem trabalhos de campo realizados pelos profissionais.

Entre os trabalhos desenvolvidos no local estão iniciativas relacionadas à conservação da onça-pintada e ao monitoramento de aves, incluindo a arara-azul. Entre eles o Onçafari, o Instituto Arara-Azul, o Projeto Papagaio-Verdadeiro e o Instituto Tamanduá.

A propriedade possui cerca de 53 mil hectares e foi fundada há mais de 35 anos. Segundo informações da própria fazenda, mais de 15 mil hectares da área são destinados à conservação por meio de uma reserva particular.

Leonardo Dicaprio e amigos estão na Fazenda Caiman em MS — Foto: Reprodução

DiCaprio, a namorada e os amigos estão hospedados na Villa Privativa Cordilheira, uma das opções de hospedagem da fazenda. A estrutura foi inaugurada em 2026 e funciona de forma exclusiva para um único grupo.

A villa possui sete bangalôs de 70 metros quadrados, além de áreas de convivência, piscina e sala de ginástica. A capacidade é de até 16 pessoas. O modelo de hospedagem permite que o grupo tenha carro e guia exclusivos durante a programação.

A Fazenda Caiman também possui a Casa Caiman, principal estrutura de hospedagem da propriedade, com 18 suítes, além da villa privativa Baiazinha.

As diárias incluem refeições e atividades realizadas na propriedade. Entre as opções estão caminhadas por áreas de vegetação nativa, passeios para observação de animais, saídas noturnas e passeios de canoa.

Também são oferecidas atividades com custo adicional, como cavalgadas e observação de aves.

A hospedagem prevê ainda uma contribuição ambiental de R$ 500 por pessoa, por estadia, segundo informações divulgadas pela Fazenda Caiman.

De acordo com o estabelecimento, o valor é destinado à manutenção de projetos de conservação e da Reserva Particular do Patrimônio Natural (RPPN) Dona Aracy.

Entre as iniciativas que atuam na Fazenda Caiman está o Onçafari, projeto voltado à conservação da onça-pintada. A atividade desenvolvida no local permite o acompanhamento de trabalhos realizados por biólogos e pesquisadores que monitoram os animais e estudam seu comportamento.

Outro projeto com atuação na propriedade é o Instituto Arara-Azul, que desenvolve pesquisas e ações de conservação da espécie no Pantanal. Entre as atividades realizadas estão o acompanhamento do comportamento das aves e o monitoramento de ninhos.

Segundo o Instituto Arara-Azul, o trabalho desenvolvido ao longo das últimas décadas contribuiu para a ampliação do conhecimento sobre a espécie e para ações de conservação da arara-azul no Pantanal.

A Fazenda Caiman informa que mais de 500 espécies já foram registradas na área, entre elas onças-pintadas, tamanduás-bandeira e aproximadamente 340 espécies de aves.

A Fazenda Caiman fica em Miranda, no Pantanal de Mato Grosso do Sul. Segundo informações divulgadas pela propriedade, o local está a aproximadamente 236 quilômetros do Aeroporto Internacional de Campo Grande e a 182 quilômetros de Bonito.

Por estrada, o deslocamento informado é de aproximadamente 3h30 a partir de Campo Grande e 2h30 partindo de Bonito.

A propriedade também possui uma pista de pouso particular para aeronaves de pequeno porte. O trajeto aéreo entre Campo Grande e a fazenda é estimado em cerca de uma hora.

Os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão cumpriram agendas de campanha nesta segunda-feira (31), com compromissos em São Luís e em municípios do interior do estado. André Luís (Missão), Orleans Brandão ( MDB ) e Reginaldo Lima ( PCB ) participaram de ações de campanha.

Durante as agendas, os candidatos apresentaram propostas voltadas à geração de emprego e renda no Maranhão.

A TV Mirante acompanhou os compromissos dos candidatos e registrou as principais propostas apresentadas por cada um ao longo do dia.

Veja, abaixo, como foi o dia do candidato André Luís (Missão):

Eleições 2026: saiba como foi o dia do candidato André Luís ao governo do Maranhão — Foto: Reprodução/TV Mirante

O candidato ao governo do Maranhão André Luís (Missão) cumpriu agenda de campanha nesta segunda-feira (31), em Caxias , no Leste do estado. Pela manhã, o empresário esteve no Centro da cidade, onde entregou panfletos e conversou com trabalhadores sobre desafios e demandas da população caxiense.

Candidato ao governo do Maranhão pela primeira vez, André Luís tem 41 anos e é empresário. Durante a agenda, ele apresentou propostas voltadas para a geração de emprego e renda no estado.

Ao falar sobre desenvolvimento econômico, o candidato defendeu a industrialização do interior do Maranhão como uma das principais medidas para ampliar as oportunidades de trabalho e fortalecer a economia dos municípios.

André Luís reforçou que pretende levar investimentos para o interior do estado a partir das características econômicas de cada região.

“Nossa proposta para o governo do Maranhão é foco e na industrialização e na interiorização da atividade econômica. Caxias, em especial, tem muito a contribuir pelo seu aprendizado, lembrando que saiu daqui também do município de Codó, o boom econômico do Maranhão entre 1720 e 1880 por meio do algodão. E o que nós aprendemos com isso é que a industrialização é o único caminho para de fato, o enriquecimento do interior do nosso estado. Nós não podemos focar só no comércio, só em trabalhos conectados com a prefeitura. A pauta do partido Missão é a industrialização. Nós precisamos fazer com que o grão que passa pelas nossas estradas aqui pertinho, a 135, é a BR-316, fazer com que esse grão se desenvolva aqui no município de Caxias, gerando trabalho e renda com a melhor qualidade, lembrando que os melhores empregos estão na indústria e essa é a proposta do partido Missão para todo o estado do Maranhão”, afirmou.

articles.title: Ceredigion family's fear for hydropower worker missing after Nepal flood
articles.summary: Jit Bahadur Chaudhary was working at the hydropower site when the flood hit on Wednesday.
articles.body:
A woman in Wales says she has "lost hope" as she awaits news of a family member in Nepal who is missing following the massive flash flood last week .

Jyoti Upadhyay, who is from Nepal but has lived in Tal-y-bont in Ceredigion for the past five years, said she and her husband had not been able to find out anything about the whereabouts of hydropower station worker Jit Bahadur Chaudhary.

Chaudhary, who is not a blood relation but is considered family by Upadhyay as he has lived with her mother-in-law for the past 25 years, was working at the Trishuli 3B site in the Bagmati Province.

"To be honest, since Saturday we have lost hope," said Upadhyay.

On Monday morning, 933 hydropower workers from sites across Nepal were missing - in total, 4,247 people were unaccounted for, with at least 903 known to have died.

Authorities have said rescue efforts have been largey focussed on the Trishuli 3A and 3B sites - hydropower projects with tunnels.

Nepali authorities are blasting into hillsides to try and reach those trapped, with a controlled blast carried out at the Trishuli site in an attempt to open up access in the early hours of Monday.

"It has been extremely difficult to reach the site. What we understand is that all the buildings are under meters of mud and it has been impossible to search for anyone there," Upadhyay told BBC Radio Cymru's Bwrw Golwg programme .

"Within 20 minutes the connections were all down. The phone signals have not been working and that is why it has been so difficult to hear anything.

"It took about three days for us to get any information. We have been looking at the news, trying local contacts and trying to see what the army and the police have been doing."

She continued: "We know that the only way to reach the site is by helicopter. You need special skills to be able to drive a helicopter in that area. It is an extremely difficult place. We have been waiting for special machines to be able to work through the mud.

"There is some good news from other stations along the river as some people were able to hide in tunnels within the hydropower stations .

"There's not a lot of hope for that particular site - but we don't know until someone can get in. At the moment everything is under mud."

The disaster was caused by a "glacial collapse" , which is when a glacier or part of a glacier disintegrates, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS).

The collapsed glacier hit the bottom of a valley so powerfully that it registered a tremor with a magnitude of 5.2, according to the agency.

This caused "subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream" - powerful floodwaters and debris travelled some 62 miles (100km).

Upadhyay explained that some tourists were among those missing, because the "area is important for pilgrimage to many religions".

She added the region was used to natural disasters, but that no one had expected flooding on this scale.

"In Nepal, we know that earthquakes can happen [but] this is worse than what has happened before," she said, adding the main concern was rising temperatures causing "more cases of glaciers melting and collapsing".

articles.title: Lowestoft rollercoaster beaks down with 27 people being rescued
articles.summary: Crews spend more than three hours bringing people down from the ride in Lowestoft.
articles.body:
Firefighters have rescued 27 people who were stuck on a rollercoaster for up to three hours.

Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service said it was called to the Wipeout ride at Pleasurewood Hills in Lowestoft at 13:36 BST.

An eyewitness described what appeared to be a power cut affecting multiple rides at the attraction, and video footage showed the moment the carriages came to a stop about 15m (49ft) in the air.

Pleasurewood Hills said it was "incredibly grateful for the way [the riders] handled" the situation and to their families for their "understanding and patience".

"We appreciate that being stuck on a ride is not something anyone expects when visiting us."

Park visitor Richard Lines said he was on another ride close to Wipeout, when a power cut appeared to affect multiple rides.

Lines said he saw a worker subsequently tending to the ride, which was stationary, and this moment can be seen in video footage shared with the BBC.

The carriages then begin moving again, but within seconds, they can be seen slowly rolling back and forth, before coming to a standstill.

Lines said the fire service used an aerial ladder to free the passengers one-by-one.

"You feel sorry for the ones that were either at the front or the back who were up there for a good three hours - which is a long time," said Lines, from Wymondham in Norfolk, who was visiting with his two children.

The fire service said by 17:10 they had rescued all 27 passengers and that no-one was injured.

Bank Holiday Monday is the last day of the summer season for the theme park, which extended the day's opening hours to reflect this.

Wipeout was launched as a park ride in 2007 and was then described as "the tallest, fastest and most extreme ride in East Anglia".

It underwent a £1m transformation over the winter of 2024-2025, the website says, including a new train with waist restraint lap bars for improved comfort and safety.

A man was rescued from the ride in 2017 after it broke down.

Pleasurewood Hills also said the "safety and wellbeing of our guests is always our highest priority".

They "sincerely apologised" to the visitors affected, and said they would receive complimentary tickets as compensation.

articles.summary: The bunkered Natanz structure was built between 2010 and 2017, raising urgent questions about Iran's uranium enrichment capabilities after two wars.
articles.body: A new report from a leading think tank has revealed what it says is a partially submerged Iranian uranium facility at the Natanz nuclear compound in Iran. The revelation of the secretive facility raises new concerns over whether Iran’s nuclear weapons apparatus was destroyed during the two American-Israeli-launched wars against the regime in 2025 and 2026. Since the June 2025 war, no vehicle activity has been observed at the facility in available satellite imagery." According to the institute, "The Institute has identified a separately enclosed, partially below-ground, bunkered building at the Natanz Nuclear Complex that was likely intended to serve as uranium hexafluoride… storage facility to support large-scale uranium enrichment at the Natanz Fuel Enrichment Plant. The bunkered structure was constructed between 2010 and 2017, with the bulk of construction occurring between 2015 and 2017." It further added that "The lesson for today is that any temporary enrichment ban must include a dismantlement and dissolution of remaining capabilities and must not allow for any type of preparatory activity for the end of a ban." According to another report by the Institute for Science and International Security in April," From December 2024 to June 2025, a half-year period, Iran almost doubled its stock of 60% enriched uranium to 440 kilograms. This action dramatically increased suspicion that Iran was moving toward a decision to build nuclear weapons, significantly shortening timelines to be able to create a nuclear arsenal with up to ten nuclear weapons." The U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran’s vast nuclear weapons facility during Operation Midnight Hammer in June 2025 significantly set back Iran’s ability to produce atomic weapons and enrich uranium. OBAMA-ERA INSPECTION FLAWS IN IRAN COULD PERSIST AS EXPERTS WARN OF NUCLEAR BLIND SPOTS Jason Brodsky, policy director at United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI), told Fox News Digital that "The report assesses the structure at the Natanz nuclear facility was not targeted during Operations Midnight Hammer and Epic Fury. This raises questions as to why the U.S. and Israel did not target the site. Given that Iran is not allowing IAEA [International Atomic Energy Agency] inspections of bombed facilities, in contravention of its NPT [Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons]obligations, this will require Washington and Jerusalem to rely on their own intelligence estimates as to this bunkered building." Brodsky added, "If it is still intact and can accommodate this kind of enrichment activity, the site should be destroyed in any future strikes. The allowance of such a facility under the JCPOA [Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action] demonstrates the flaws of the agreement — permitting Iran to retain an industrial scale enrichment program following the sunsets of various provisions — and underscores why zero enrichment in Iran has to continue to be the international demand." When asked about the facility and if the IAEA plans to inspect it, Fredrik Dahl, a spokesman for the IAEA, told Fox News Digital, that "The building you are referring to is well-known to the Agency as part of the Natanz site that the IAEA regularly inspected prior to mid-2025." Asked about the report, Anna Kelly, a White House spokeswoman, told Fox News Digital that "First, Iran’s nuclear facilities were totally obliterated during Operation Midnight Hammer. articles.title: Built in 1743, this 1,050-acre Maryland farm became a War of 1812 battlefield where bullets and buckles remained buried for two centuries; the family now plans to sell
articles.summary: US News: A 1,050-acre historic farm in Chestertown, Maryland, built in 1743 and kept in the same family for generations, has been put up for sale, according to.
articles.body: A 1,050-acre historic farm in Chestertown, Maryland, built in 1743 and kept in the same family for generations, has been put up for sale, according to a real estate report by The Wall Street Journal. The large Eastern Shore property has strong links to American history. During the War of 1812, it was the site of the Battle of Caulk's Field, where Maryland militia fought British forces in late August 1814. For more than 200 years, physical remains of the battle, including musket balls, uniform buckles and pieces of military equipment, have remained buried across the farm.Historic home and centuries-old landscapeThe main house was built in 1743, more than 30 years before the American Revolutionary War. Built in the colonial style common across the Mid-Atlantic, the brick home was expanded over the centuries but has retained much of its original design, timber beams and historic masonry. The 1,050-acre estate includes working farmland, mature woodland and access to waterways connected to the Chesapeake Bay watershed. The property is one of the largest remaining areas of connected colonial-era land in Kent County, Maryland. During the 18th and 19th centuries, the land was used as a working plantation and farm. It produced crops including tobacco, wheat and corn. Because the property stayed within the same family for generations, large parts of the landscape were never heavily changed by modern development.Key milestones of the historic estateThe Battle of Caulk's FieldOn the night of 31 August 1814, the farm became the scene of a major battle during the Chesapeake Campaign of the War of 1812. British Royal Navy forces under Captain Sir Peter Parker of HMS Menelaus launched a night raid. The operation was meant to draw Maryland militia away while larger British forces targeted Baltimore and Washington, D.C. Lieutenant Colonel Philip Reed led about 170 men from the 21st Maryland Regiment. They took defensive positions on a high ridge on the property known as Caulk's Field.More than 100 British sailors and marines moved across the open fields under moonlight. American forces responded with musket fire and field artillery. The British landing party eventually retreated, and Captain Parker was killed during the fighting. The battle became one of the few land victories achieved by local militia forces on Maryland's Eastern Shore during the 1814 campaign.Discoveries beneath the soilThe battlefield remained in agricultural use for generations instead of being covered by roads or buildings. This helped preserve objects from the battle beneath the soil for more than two centuries. Archaeological investigations and metal-detector surveys carried out in recent decades have uncovered many objects linked to the 1814 fight. Researchers found dropped lead musket balls, fired grape shot, military brass belt buckles, uniform buttons and iron equipment. By mapping where the objects were found, historians were able to better understand how the battle unfolded. The discoveries helped researchers identify the positions of American militia units and British forces, as well as their firing lines and retreat routes across the fields.Family ownership comes to an endThe decision to sell the 1,050-acre property marks an important change for the Chestertown landmark. As noted in The Wall Street Journal's real estate report, large historic properties that combine extensive farmland, important history and recognised battlefield sites rarely become available on the luxury property market. Local conservation and historic preservation groups are watching the sale closely. They want to see whether a future owner will maintain existing conservation protections and continue using the land for agriculture. The combination of historic importance, farmland and preserved open space makes the property one of the notable historic real estate offerings in the Mid-Atlantic region. The sale includes the original 1743 manor house, additional buildings, farming facilities and the historic battlefield land where the Battle of Caulk's Field took place.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: US Streamers News: Dalauan “LowTierGod” Sparrow, better known as LTG, is back in the spotlight after an old post about his streaming career resurfaced on social media. T.
articles.body: Dalauan “LowTierGod” Sparrow, better known as LTG, is back in the spotlight after an old post about his streaming career resurfaced on social media. The post, made in August 2020, said LTG would consider himself a “failure in life” if he was still mainly streaming six years later instead of moving into areas such as acting. That six-year period has now ended, sending the so-called “Doomsdale” countdown to zero. Users have since brought the old statement back and asked LTG whether he believes his prediction came true. LTG responded with a short message of his own.LowTierGod’s old six-year prediction comes backThe “Doomsdale” discussion comes from a post LTG made in August 2020. He had set himself a six-year deadline and suggested that continuing to primarily stream after that point would mean he had failed to move forward with his life.Now that six years have passed, users have revived the post and started asking LTG about his prediction.X user @FearedBuck highlighted the moment, writing:“Doomsdale is officially in 2 hours. Six years ago, LowTierGod said that if he was still primarily streaming instead of moving on to things like acting, he would consider himself a ‘failure in life.’”Other users also tagged LTG and asked whether he believed he had reached the point he described six years ago.The discussion has focused on whether LTG actually remained limited to streaming. His career since the original post suggests that his online work has continued across several platforms, while he has also taken part in projects outside livestreaming.LTG himself responded to the renewed attention with a brief message:“Never tell the world your dreams.”He did not directly say whether he considers himself to have failed under the terms of his 2020 statement.LowTierGod has continued working outside regular livestreamsLTG still has a sizeable online audience. His Twitch account has around 324,000 followers, while his Instagram has roughly 112,000. He also has about 70,000 followers on Kick and more than 36,000 YouTube subscribers.His work has not been limited to livestreaming either. LTG appeared in the 2025 comedy-drama film Back to Bridgewood, giving him a feature-film credit outside his usual streaming work.He has also developed his own merchandise brand, Covenant. In addition, LTG appeared at The Streamer Awards 2024, where he presented the Best Fighting Games Streamer award to Etoiles.Those activities matter because the original 2020 post specifically mentioned moving into areas such as acting. While LTG remains active as a streamer, he has also made moves into other forms of entertainment and business.The renewed “Doomsdale” debate therefore comes down to how LTG views his own six-year goal. By the exact wording of his old post, he had set streaming as something he wanted to move beyond. Six years later, streaming is still a major part of his career, but it is not the only thing he has pursued.The countdown reaching zero has given social media users a reason to revisit a prediction LTG made years ago. His latest response, however, leaves the question of whether he considers that prediction fulfilled or broken open to interpretation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Florida bans Flock cameras days after a sheriff's deputy resigns for misusing AI cameras to track ex-girlfriend
articles.summary: US News: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis announced Monday that he is removing Flock cameras from state roadways. The order said all Flock cameras were to be remo.
articles.body: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis announced Monday that he is removing Flock cameras from state roadways. The order said all Flock cameras were to be removed from what he calls the “state highway system” within the next 30 days, which would include interstates like I-10 and I-75. That order led to several sheriff’s departments like in Franklin, Liberty and Putnam Counties to announce they’re ending their own license plate reader programs. After 30 days, if there are Flock cameras still found on some roads, Florida's Department of Transportation will take them down. The memo also said that Flock cameras will not get permits in Florida in the future as well.Citing the cases of cops stalking their ex-girlfriends using the surveillance system, Ron DeSantis said his administration is pro-law enforcement. “But, you also have to say, okay, how could this be misused? And how could a private company misuse the data, but also law enforcement? We know there was an officer in Florida who was using the LPR data to track like an ex-girlfriend or something like that,” DeSantis said.Deputy of the Year 2025 resigns over stalking ex-girlfriend using Flock, claim reportsThe Florida Governor's order came days after a Florida sheriff's deputy who was named “2025 Deputy of the Year” had to resign after an internal investigation revealed “egregious misconduct”, including an improper search of his ex-girlfriend’s license plate, photos involving a firearm during a sex act and an apparent Nazi salute. Michael Fultz resigned from the Brevard County Sheriff’s Office as the agency prepared to fire him, several local media outlets like News 6, WESH and 404 Media reported.Fultz’s ex-girlfriend contacted the sheriff’s office with numerous allegations on the same day he was formally honored as “2025 Deputy of the Year” in March 2026.“My intention in providing this information is not to pursue personal retaliation but to ensure the agency is aware of conduct that, in my understanding, may conflict with departmental policies or professional standards,” she said. The sheriff’s office subsequently audited its Flock Safety license-plate reader system and found that Fultz had searched his ex-girlfriend’s license plate once before the beginning of his shift. The search was categorized as an “investigation,”“Deputy Fultz denied checking her vehicle registration to spy on her or out of revenge but could not provide any reason as to why he queried her vehicle registration tag while off duty,” investigators wrote, according to News 6.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Polluted Stiebeuel River water transformed into irrigation supply using stones, sand and heat-treated wood; University of Cape Town project treats 36,000 litres daily and removes 99% of toxins
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A simple combination of stones, sand and heat-treated wood is helping transform heavily polluted river water in South Africa into water clean enough t.
articles.body: A simple combination of stones, sand and heat-treated wood is helping transform heavily polluted river water in South Africa into water clean enough to irrigate vegetable gardens and support food production in a growing informal settlement.Researchers from the University of Cape Town are using a nature-based filtration system to treat around 36,000 litres of water from the Stiebeuel River every day.The river has been contaminated by sewage, chemicals and traces of drugs and pharmaceutical waste. But after passing through the treatment system, a portion of the water is now being used to irrigate community vegetable plots in Langrug, near Stellenbosch in South Africa’s Western Cape.The project, known as the Water Hub, does not rely on chemical treatment and operates using renewable solar energy.Scientists behind the initiative believe the approach could offer a potential model for helping vulnerable communities improve food security as climate change increases pressure on water supplies.Polluted river water now helping grow foodKevin Winter, one of the researchers behind the Water Hub project, told The Guardian that the treated water is already making a tangible difference to people living in Langrug.“What we’re doing is taking that water, treating it every day, and some of that water is now being used for growing vegetables, for feeding hungry children and people living in the informal settlement,” Winter said.He said the quality of the treated water has improved dramatically.“You’d be very hard pressed to know the difference between it and your municipal treated water, which has been through a treatment plant and been chlorinated,” he said.The water is not considered safe for drinking, but the project has reached a significant milestone this year by reducing bacteria and pathogens to levels suitable for irrigation.The system now removes about 99% of toxins, according to Winter, before most of the treated water is released back into the river, where it can contribute to surrounding ecosystems.Around 3,000 litres is retained for irrigating food-producing gardens at the Water Hub.How the natural filtration system worksThe Water Hub was established in 2018 on the site of an abandoned wastewater facility.Researchers repurposed old wastewater drying beds and transformed them into a series of filtration cells.The system operates off-grid and uses solar power to pump polluted river water into the cells, where it gradually passes through different natural filtration materials over approximately five days.The first stage uses large stones to trap particles and some chemicals.The water then passes through biochar — wood heated to around 800C (1,470F) — which helps remove contaminants including traces of drugs, pharmaceutical waste and ammonia.Finally, smaller stones and layers of sand help absorb remaining pollutants before the treated water is released or diverted for irrigation.The approach is relatively simple, but researchers say it can make a significant difference in communities that lack access to conventional water infrastructure.Langrug's population has rapidly expandedThe need for such an alternative has become increasingly urgent in Langrug.Winter has worked in the area since 2006 and has witnessed its population increase dramatically, from around 3,000 people to more than 26,000.Much of the growth has been driven by seasonal employment on farms and in nearby Franschhoek, a wealthy town in the Western Cape.The rapid, largely unplanned expansion of Langrug left many residents without reliable access to clean water and adequate sewage facilities.Existing water infrastructure struggled to cope with the growing population, prompting Winter and his colleagues to explore another approach.Rather than building an entirely new conventional treatment facility, they transformed an abandoned wastewater site into a nature-based treatment system.Why the project matters amid climate changeThe initiative comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over water scarcity across the Western Cape and beyond.In 2018, the region experienced an extreme water crisis after an extended drought pushed reservoirs dangerously close to running dry.For months, households were forced to ration their water supplies, while around 31,000 farm workers lost their jobs.For Winter, such experiences underline why communities need to find new ways of securing both water and food in a changing climate.“It’s absolutely crucial that we start looking at how we do this,” he said.“Climate in the next 30 years, particularly in our region here, is going to look very, very different.”He warned that the region could face a combination of climate-related threats, including wildfires, flooding and prolonged droughts that could leave communities struggling to access both water and food.A solution for communities, not citiesWinter stressed that the Water Hub is not intended to replace conventional wastewater treatment facilities capable of processing industrial-scale volumes for large towns and cities.Instead, the project is designed around the needs of rural and vulnerable communities where conventional infrastructure may be expensive, difficult or impractical to build.The combination of solar energy and natural filtration also means the system can operate without relying on chemical treatment.For the community around the Water Hub, the impact is already tangible: polluted water that was once a threat is now helping grow vegetables and support local food production.“Making water available for food, and for food security, as a climate-change strategy is absolutely crucial worldwide and we’ve got to learn to be able to do that more and more,” Winter said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis closing arguments: Jury urged to convict in 1996 Tupac murder
articles.summary: In closing arguments, prosecutors said Davis’ 2019 memoir provided enough proof, while Davis’ attorney said the prosecution failed to back up Davis’ claims with clear evidence.
articles.body: A prosecutor urged jurors Monday to convict Duane “Keffe D” Davis of first-degree murder in the 1996 killing of Tupac Shakur, arguing that Davis’ own words and a case “drenched in circumstantial evidence” prove he orchestrated the drive-by shooting. Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal told jurors that Davis acquired a gun and “went hunting” for Shakur and Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight after they beat up Davis’ nephew earlier that night. Palal acknowledged that Davis’ accounts of the killing evolved over the years but argued those differences reflected Davis’ changing motivations and efforts to protect himself. One critical detail, he said, remained consistent: Davis repeatedly placed himself inside the white Cadillac from which the shots were fired. “The core facts remain. The material facts remain,” Palal said. Palal told jurors that if they believe Davis’ statements, they do not have to be independently corroborated with additional evidence. Still, Palal pointed to the rivalry between the South Side Compton Crips and Mob Piru, the fight with Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson and testimony that members of Shakur’s circle identified Anderson and Davis as suspects the night of the shooting. “Who fired is not the question,” Palal said. Prosecutors haven’t argued that Davis pulled the trigger, but instead that he was criminally responsible because he provided the gun and ordered the attack. “The shot caller doesn’t just ride along,” Palal said. Palal also argued the shooting was premeditated, pointing to testimony and Davis’ accounts that the group initially searched for Shakur before later spotting him on the road and making a U-turn. “It’s a plan, not an impulse,” Palal said. Davis, 63, faces a single count of murder with a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang in the killing of Shakur in Las Vegas nearly 30 years ago. A panel of 16 jurors, four of whom will be alternates, heard testimony from 24 prosecution witnesses and three defense witnesses over nine days. The trial was expected to take longer, with prosecutors originally planning to call 35 to 45 witnesses. The prosecution hammered home the argument that Davis called the shots for the attack on Shakur that night based on Davis’ book and interviews, while Davis’ defense attorney reiterated his claim that the prosecution’s narrative is fiction and that they failed to back up Davis’ claims with evidence. The trial brings to a head a decades-long case that for years has drawn the eyes of hip-hop fans and true crime experts alike. Shakur, who was considered one of the most influential rappers of all time, was in Las Vegas on Sept. 7, 1996, and stopped at a red light when a white Cadillac pulled up beside him, and shots were fired. Shakur died six days later from his wounds. Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight was also wounded but survived. For years, nobody had been charged in the rapper’s death until Davis began making public statements, saying he was in the Cadillac and gave the gun to others in the back seat. Davis described the shooting as an act of retaliation after Knight and Shakur’s entourage beat up Davis’ nephew hours before the shooting. Under Nevada law, someone who helps another person commit murder can be convicted of the crime. Davis is the only person still alive who was in the Cadillac. Davis’ own words are front and center Palal held up Davis’ 2019 memoir, “Compton Street Legend,” and played an interview in which Davis encouraged people to buy it to get the “real truth.” Although the book contains a disclaimer saying some facts were changed, Palal argued that names, hotels and other details changed while the central account did not. Palal also rejected the defense’s contention that Davis fabricated his accounts to make money. “It is an entirely different proposition to be profiting from a murder,” Palal said. “And that is what Mr. Davis is doing.” Davis’ defense attorney Michael Sanft also turned to his client’s memoir during his closing argument. While reading an excerpt, he said the N-word aloud, prompting people watching in an overflow courtroom to recoil and shake their heads. In multiple interviews, Davis said he handed the gun to the back seat, but in others as well as in his book, Davis wouldn’t say who pulled the trigger. The prosecution’s witnesses included a gang expert who described Davis as the shot caller that younger gang members had to obey. Witnesses also testified to the heated gang rivalry between the South Side Compton Crips and Mob Piru, which were associated with dueling record companies Bad Boy Records and Death Row Records. Lack of physical evidence, defense says Sanft has told jurors that his client’s words were braggadocio and were meant to make Davis money, not to tell the truth. Sanft, who took on the case without pay, argues there is a lack of physical evidence tying Davis to the crime, such as phone records or bills. During the trial, investigators said a Las Vegas hotel bill was found at Davis’ residence during a police search, but it wasn’t clear when it was dated — or where that evidence is currently located. The case is nearly 30 years old, which has affected the kind of evidence presented in court. Prosecutors warned jurors that material collected in the ’90s is different from what law enforcement collects today, including hotel surveillance video from the night of the shooting.
